property_summary: After calling NETM() by the owner, the owner's balance equals totalDistributed (reference preserves assigning totalDistributed to balances[owner]); the mutant that sets balances[owner]=0 breaks this by making the owner's balance possibly zero for some inputs.

Calling NETM() as the owner must set balances[owner] to totalDistributed (i.e., NETM only updates the current owner account); the mutant that omits reassigning owner to msg.sender causes NETM() invoked by the original owner to update a different (previous) owner account, breaking that invariant for some callers.

Calling NETM() by any address X always results in balances[X] == totalDistributed in the reference (because owner is set to msg.sender before assigning balances), whereas the mutant that omits owner = msg.sender may assign totalDistributed to a different address (the stored owner), so there exists an address X for which balances[X] != totalDistributed after NETM().

For any caller addr, invoking NETM() on the correct contract makes balances[caller] equal totalDistributed (because NETM sets owner = msg.sender before assigning balances[owner] = totalDistributed); the mutant that removes owner = msg.sender can leave balances[caller] != totalDistributed for some caller.

For any caller addr, after calling NETM() the reference contract ensures balances[owner] == totalDistributed where owner is set to the caller inside NETM(); the mutant that removes the assignment can leave balances[caller] != totalDistributed for some caller, so the invariant 'after NETM by caller, balances[caller] == totalDistributed' holds for the reference but is violated by the mutant for some inputs.
